text.p: Following are the main stories in Slovenia's Thursday morning newspapers.

- President of the European Commission Jacques Santer said the six countries that are likely to be invited to start negotiations of full membership in the European Union next year, including Slovenia, must undertake further reforms before being accepted.
- The government named new controlling boards of state-owned banks Nova Ljubljanska Banka and Nova Kreditna Banka Maribor.
- Agricultural Minister Ciril Smrkolj said the government would help farmers in Pomurje in eastern Slovenia whose crop was destroyed by hail earlier this month.
- German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek who met in Bonn on Wednesday said relations between the two countries were very good.
- The State Council, upper house of parliament, vetoed a new notary law according to which real estate contracts would only be legal if written by a lawyer.
- Trader Kovinotehna said it would pay no dividend for 1996.
- Parliamentary board for the economy said the government should prepare a law to protect small shareholders.
